```{r}
#| label: load-packages-r
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(nanoparquet)
library(tidymodels)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

# The factor zoo of lectures 10 and 11
sample_start <- ymd("1973-01-01")
sample_end <- ymd("2023-12-31")
test_start <- ymd("2000-01-01")
n_folds <- 5
ridge_lambdas <- 10^seq(-7, -1, by = 0.25)
lasso_lambdas <- 10^seq(-6, -2.5, by = 0.25)

# Factors: up to 60, a few-factor model in the text; the weight on the means
# of Lettau & Pelger (2020)
max_factors <- 60
few_factors <- 5
phi_rp <- 10
phis <- c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100)

months_per_year <- 12

# Principal components in the figure on variance and premia
n_components_shown <- 30

# Sample periods in labels, e.g. 1973–1999
estimation_years <- paste0(year(sample_start), "–", year(test_start) - 1)
test_years <- paste0(year(test_start), "–", year(sample_end))

# Sharpe ratios in the text: none (–) for a negative mean excess return, since
# more volatility would then raise the Sharpe ratio
sharpe_text <- function(x) if_else(x > 0, number(x, 0.01), "–")

# Colours of the slides, used by the figures
ku_red <- "#901A1E"
jet <- "#3d3d3d"
grey <- "#666666"
light <- "#e6e3df"
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
)

source("lecture-slides/_live-poll.R")
validation_survey <- "aef27-validation-scheme"
```

```{python}
#| label: load-packages-py

import numpy as np
```

```{r}
#| label: lectures-10-and-11-code
#| include: false
# The data, the metric, the workflows and the folds of lectures 10 and 11
osap_url <- paste0(
  "https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/resolve/",
  "Data-Release-2026.10/Portfolios/Full%20Sets%20OP/PredictorLSretWide.parquet"
)
osap_file <- "data/osap_long_short_returns.parquet"
if (!file.exists(osap_file)) {
  download.file(osap_url, osap_file, mode = "wb")
}
anomalies <- read_parquet(osap_file) |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end)) |>
  select(date, where(\(x) !anyNA(x))) |>
  mutate(across(-date, \(x) x / 100), y = 1)
anomaly_names <- setdiff(names(anomalies), c("date", "y"))
sample_split <- make_splits(
  filter(anomalies, date < test_start),
  assessment = filter(anomalies, date >= test_start)
)
estimation_months <- training(sample_split)
test_months <- testing(sample_split)
x_estimation <- as.matrix(estimation_months[anomaly_names])
x_test <- as.matrix(test_months[anomaly_names])

sharpe_ratio_vec <- function(truth, estimate, ...) {
  mean(estimate) / sd(estimate) * sqrt(months_per_year)
}
sharpe_ratio <- function(data, truth, estimate, ...) {
  numeric_metric_summarizer(
    "sharpe_ratio",
    sharpe_ratio_vec,
    data,
    !!enquo(truth),
    !!enquo(estimate)
  )
}
sharpe_ratio <- new_numeric_metric(sharpe_ratio, direction = "maximize")
sharpe_in <- function(fit, months) {
  augment(fit, months) |> sharpe_ratio(y, .pred) |> pull(.estimate)
}
# Sharpe ratios of a fitted workflow in both samples, for figures and tables
sample_sharpe <- function(fit) {
  c(
    estimation = sharpe_in(fit, estimation_months),
    test = sharpe_in(fit, test_months)
  )
}
# The same for weights from a function of our own, as in lecture 11
weights_sharpe <- function(weights) {
  c(
    estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = drop(x_estimation %*% weights)),
    test = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = drop(x_test %*% weights))
  )
}

plug_in_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = y, predictors = all_of(anomaly_names)) |>
  add_model(linear_reg(), formula = y ~ 0 + .)
ridge_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 0) |>
  set_engine(
    "glmnet",
    intercept = FALSE,
    standardize = FALSE,
    path_values = ridge_lambdas,
    control = list(thresh = 1e-12)
  )
ridge_workflow <- update_model(plug_in_workflow, ridge_model)
lasso_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) |>
  set_engine(
    "glmnet",
    intercept = FALSE,
    standardize = FALSE,
    path_values = lasso_lambdas,
    control = list(thresh = 1e-12)
  )
lasso_workflow <- update_model(plug_in_workflow, lasso_model)

market <- read_parquet("data/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end))
market_sharpe <- c(
  estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(
    estimate = market$mkt_excess[market$date < test_start]
  ),
  test = sharpe_ratio_vec(
    estimate = market$mkt_excess[market$date >= test_start]
  )
)
equal_sharpe <- c(
  estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(
    estimate = rowMeans(estimation_months[anomaly_names])
  ),
  test = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = rowMeans(test_months[anomaly_names]))
)
plug_in_sharpe <- sample_sharpe(fit(plug_in_workflow, estimation_months))

# k = 5 consecutive blocks of the estimation months as folds
block_folds <- estimation_months |>
  mutate(block = ceiling(dense_rank(date) / (n_distinct(date) / n_folds))) |>
  group_vfold_cv(group = block, v = n_folds)
```

```{r}
#| label: lecture-11-tuning
#| include: false
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr list(ridge_lambdas, lasso_lambdas, n_folds, sample_start, sample_end, test_start)
# Ridge, the lasso on anomalies and the lasso on principal components, each
# with the penalty chosen by cross-validation as in lecture 11
ridge_tuning <- tune_grid(
  ridge_workflow,
  block_folds,
  grid = tibble(penalty = ridge_lambdas),
  metrics = metric_set(sharpe_ratio)
)
ridge_fit <- ridge_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(select_best(ridge_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")) |>
  fit(estimation_months)
lasso_tuning <- tune_grid(
  lasso_workflow,
  block_folds,
  grid = tibble(penalty = lasso_lambdas),
  metrics = metric_set(sharpe_ratio)
)
lasso_fit <- lasso_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(select_best(lasso_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")) |>
  fit(estimation_months)
ridge_sharpe <- sample_sharpe(ridge_fit)
lasso_sharpe <- sample_sharpe(lasso_fit)
lasso_kept <- sum(tidy(lasso_fit)$estimate != 0)

pc_lasso_weights <- function(months, lambda) {
  x <- as.matrix(months[anomaly_names])
  components <- eigen(cov(x), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
  lasso_fit <- lasso_model |>
    finalize_model(tibble(penalty = lambda)) |>
    fit_xy(as.data.frame(x %*% components), months$y)
  components %*% tidy(lasso_fit)$estimate[-1]
}
pc_lasso_cv <- map_dbl(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) {
  map_dbl(block_folds$splits, \(split) {
    weights <- pc_lasso_weights(analysis(split), lambda)
    validation <- assessment(split)
    portfolio_returns <- as.matrix(validation[anomaly_names]) %*% weights
    sharpe_ratio_vec(validation$y, portfolio_returns[, 1])
  }) |>
    mean()
})
pc_lasso_lambda <- lasso_lambdas[which.max(pc_lasso_cv)]
# The lasso on the components of the whole estimation sample
components_estimation <- eigen(cov(x_estimation), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
pc_lasso_fit <- function(lambda) {
  lasso_model |>
    finalize_model(tibble(penalty = lambda)) |>
    fit_xy(
      as.data.frame(x_estimation %*% components_estimation),
      estimation_months$y
    )
}
pc_weights <- tidy(pc_lasso_fit(pc_lasso_lambda))$estimate[-1]
pc_kept <- sum(pc_weights != 0)
pc_lasso_sharpe <- weights_sharpe(components_estimation %*% pc_weights)
```

## From `r length(anomaly_names)` anomalies to a few factors

- **Lecture 11:** the best SDF of the zoo needs dozens of anomalies or principal components. The SDF weights still come from `r length(anomaly_names)` means and `r comma(length(anomaly_names) * (length(anomaly_names) + 1) / 2)` covariances
- **A factor model:** a few factors drive all `r length(anomaly_names)` returns, $F_t = B f_t + e_t$. If the SDF is spanned by $f$, a handful of means and covariances suffice
- **The factors are latent:** we estimate them from the returns themselves

::: {.highlight}
**Today:** your validation schemes from exercise 7. Then which few factors: the ones that explain the most variance (principal components) or the ones that carry a premium (risk-premium PCA)? And how many?
:::

# Principal components

## Why look for the largest variance?

- **Lecture 11:** the principal components $P_{j,t} = v_j'F_t$ are portfolios of all anomalies; the lasso picked `r pc_kept` of them. Today: why they are candidates for factors
- **A factor structure** (APT, lecture 8): $F_t = B f_t + e_t$ with $k$ factors $f_t$ and errors $e_t$ that are uncorrelated with the factors and across anomalies. Then

$$
\Sigma = B\,\text{Var}(f)\,B' + \text{Var}(e)
$$

- The factors move all `r length(anomaly_names)` anomalies, each error only one. With many anomalies, the $k$ directions with the most variance (approximately) span the factors: we look for them

## Where the eigenvectors come from

::: {.box}
**Lecture 11:** the first principal component is the portfolio $v$ of the anomalies with the largest variance, $\max_v v'\Sigma v$ subject to $v'v = 1$. The next one has the largest variance among the portfolios uncorrelated with the first
:::

- **Why $v'v = 1$?** The portfolio $c\,v$ has $c^2$ times the variance of $v$: without a constraint, there is no maximum. The constraint only sets the scale
- **Still a portfolio:** the anomalies are long-short returns, so any weights $v$ give a long-short portfolio. Its scale changes neither its Sharpe ratio nor its correlations

::: {.fragment}
$$
\frac{\partial}{\partial v}\Big[v'\Sigma v - \delta\,(v'v - 1)\Big] = 2\,\Sigma v - 2\,\delta\, v = 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad \Sigma v = \delta\, v
$$

- The first-order condition with the Lagrange multiplier $\delta$: the best $v$ is an eigenvector of $\Sigma$, and its variance $v'\Sigma v = \delta\, v'v = \delta$ is the eigenvalue. So take the eigenvector with the largest eigenvalue
:::

## Eigenvectors of the covariance matrix

- $\Sigma$ has `r length(anomaly_names)` orthogonal eigenvectors $v_j$ with $v_j'v_j = 1$ and eigenvalues $\delta_1 \geq \delta_2 \geq \dots \geq 0$. Together they rebuild $\Sigma$:

$$
\Sigma = \sum_{j=1}^{`r length(anomaly_names)`} \delta_j\, v_j v_j'
$$

- The components $P_{j,t} = v_j'F_t$ are uncorrelated, and component $j$ has the variance $\delta_j$, a share $\delta_j / \sum_k \delta_k$ of the total
- The first $k$ components explain the most variance that any $k$ factors can: the best factor model in the least-squares sense
- The sign of a component is arbitrary: $-v_j$ is an eigenvector, too

## Variance is not a premium

```{r}
#| label: component-premia
#| include: false
eigen_estimation <- eigen(cov(x_estimation), symmetric = TRUE)
components <- tibble(
  component = seq_len(n_components_shown),
  variance_share = eigen_estimation$values[component] /
    sum(eigen_estimation$values),
  sharpe = map_dbl(component, \(j) {
    abs(sharpe_ratio_vec(
      estimate = x_estimation %*% eigen_estimation$vectors[, j]
    ))
  })
)

# Is the first component the market? Correlations in absolute value, since
# the sign of a component is arbitrary. The factor file dates each month by
# its first day
component_returns <- tibble(
  date = floor_date(estimation_months$date, "month"),
  first = as.vector(x_estimation %*% eigen_estimation$vectors[, 1]),
  second = as.vector(x_estimation %*% eigen_estimation$vectors[, 2])
) |>
  inner_join(market, join_by(date))
first_market <- abs(cor(component_returns$first, component_returns$mkt_excess))
first_smb <- abs(cor(component_returns$first, component_returns$smb))
second_market <- abs(cor(
  component_returns$second,
  component_returns$mkt_excess
))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-component-premia
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.6
variance_panel <- ggplot(components, aes(x = component, y = variance_share)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#b3b3b3") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(x = "Principal component", y = "Share of the variance")
sharpe_panel <- ggplot(components, aes(x = component, y = sharpe)) +
  geom_col(fill = ku_red) +
  labs(
    x = "Principal component",
    y = paste0("Sharpe ratio ", estimation_years, "\n(absolute value)"),
    caption = "Absolute values, since the sign of a component is arbitrary"
  )
variance_panel + sharpe_panel
```

- The first component explains `r percent(components$variance_share[1])` of the variance, but its Sharpe ratio is only `r number(components$sharpe[1], 0.01)`
- The first component is not the market: its correlation with the market is `r number(first_market, 0.01)`, with SMB (size) `r number(first_smb, 0.01)`, both in absolute value. The second component is closer to the market (`r number(second_market, 0.01)`)

# Risk-premium PCA

## Risk-premium PCA: variances and means

::: {.box}
Lettau & Pelger (2020): choose the factors so that they explain the variances **and** the means of the anomalies
:::

::: {.fragment}
If the factors price the anomalies (APT, lecture 8), the same loadings $B$ drive risk and return:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma &= B\,\text{Var}(f)\,B' + \text{Var}(e) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \mu = B\lambda \\
\Longrightarrow \quad \Sigma + \varphi\, \mu\mu' &= B\big(\text{Var}(f) + \varphi\,\lambda\lambda'\big)B' + \text{Var}(e)
\end{aligned}
$$

- Risk-premium PCA takes the eigenvectors of $\Sigma + \varphi\, \mu\mu'$: the same factors, but the means help to find them. $\varphi = 0$: PCA
- $\varphi > 0$: factors with a premium move up the ranking, even if their variance is small. We use $\varphi$ = `r phi_rp`, a weight of the size Lettau & Pelger use
:::

## PCA and risk-premium PCA in code

- `factor_weights()`: the first $k$ eigenvectors of $\Sigma + \varphi\,\mu\mu'$ in the months it is fitted on give the factors, then the mean-variance portfolio of the $k$ factors, $\text{Var}(f)^{-1}E[f]$
- The factors are portfolios of the anomalies, so their mean-variance portfolio is one, too. As for `pc_lasso_weights()` of lecture 11, the Sharpe ratio metric of lecture 10 evaluates its returns

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: factor-weights-r
factor_weights <- function(months, k, phi = 0) {
  x <- as.matrix(months[anomaly_names])
  mu <- colMeans(x)
  vectors <- eigen(cov(x) + phi * tcrossprod(mu), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
  loadings <- vectors[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]
  factors <- x %*% loadings
  loadings %*% solve(cov(factors), colMeans(factors))
}
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: factor-weights-py
#| eval: false
def factor_weights(x, k, phi=0.0):
    mu = x.mean(axis=0)
    values, vectors = np.linalg.eigh(np.cov(x, rowvar=False) + phi * np.outer(mu, mu))
    loadings = vectors[:, np.argsort(values)[::-1][:k]]
    factors = x @ loadings
    covariance = np.atleast_2d(np.cov(factors, rowvar=False))
    return loadings @ np.linalg.solve(covariance, factors.mean(axis=0))
```
:::

## Risk-premium PCA on the zoo

- Sharpe ratio of the mean-variance portfolio of the first $k$ factors. With one factor, risk-premium PCA reaches `r sharpe_text(rp_path$test[1])` in the test sample (PCA: `r sharpe_text(pca_path$test[1])`, a negative mean), with `r few_factors` factors `r sharpe_text(rp_path$test[few_factors])` (PCA: `r sharpe_text(pca_path$test[few_factors])`)
- With many factors the gap narrows, since both span more and more of the same space: at `r max_factors` factors, `r number(pca_path$test[max_factors], 0.01)` against `r number(rp_path$test[max_factors], 0.01)`

## How many factors?

```{r}
#| label: choose-factors-r
#| include: false
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr list(phi_rp, max_factors, n_folds, sample_start, sample_end, test_start)
# The number of factors is a tuning parameter: the folds and the metric of
# lecture 11, with a map over k as for the lasso on principal components
factor_cv <- expand_grid(phi = c(0, phi_rp), factors = seq_len(max_factors)) |>
  mutate(
    cv = map2_dbl(phi, factors, \(phi, k) {
      map_dbl(block_folds$splits, \(split) {
        weights <- factor_weights(analysis(split), k, phi)
        validation <- assessment(split)
        portfolio_returns <- as.matrix(validation[anomaly_names]) %*% weights
        sharpe_ratio_vec(validation$y, portfolio_returns[, 1])
      }) |>
        mean()
    })
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-factor-cv
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.8
factor_cv <- factor_cv |>
  mutate(method = if_else(phi == 0, "PCA", paste0("RP-PCA, φ = ", phi_rp)))
chosen_factors <- factor_cv |>
  group_by(phi) |>
  slice_max(cv) |>
  ungroup()
ggplot(factor_cv, aes(x = factors, y = cv, color = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(
    data = chosen_factors,
    size = 5,
    shape = 21,
    stroke = 1.3,
    fill = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#b3b3b3", ku_red)) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of factors",
    y = "Validation Sharpe ratio (annualized)",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Circles: number of factors chosen by cross-validation"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

- The number of factors is a tuning parameter, chosen by cross-validation with the `r n_folds` consecutive blocks and the Sharpe ratio metric of lecture 11, by hand as for the lasso on principal components
- Cross-validation picks many factors: the validation Sharpe ratio peaks at `r chosen_factors$factors[chosen_factors$phi == 0]` factors for PCA and at `r chosen_factors$factors[chosen_factors$phi == phi_rp]` for RP-PCA, out of at most `r max_factors`. As in lecture 11, the zoo has no small set of factors that does the job

## Outlook: loadings from characteristics

- PCA treats the loadings $B$ as constant. But a stock's exposure changes with its size, value or momentum
- **Instrumented PCA** (Kelly, Pruitt & Su, 2019): loadings are functions of characteristics, $\beta_{i,t} = z_{i,t}'\Gamma$, and the factors stay latent. A handful of such factors prices the cross-section of individual stocks
- **Lecture 14:** a neural network lets the SDF weights depend on characteristics in any shape

## Out-of-sample comparison

```{r}
#| label: comparison
#| echo: false

  ),
```
